summary: Georges Perrot was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1852. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1872–1883), the University of Paris (~1877–1883), and served as director of the École Normale Supérieure (~1883–1904).

Georges-Jean Pinault studied at ENS, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and EPHE under Jean Haudry (~1975–1980). Active in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, he taught at Sorbonne Nouvelle (~1980–1986), Clermont Auvergne University (~1987–1996), and became professor at EPHE in 1999.

Georgios T. Halkias, a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar, studied at the University of Hawaiʻi and Oxford under Charles Ramble (DPhil, ~2001–2006). He held research posts at SOAS, Warburg, and Bochum, and became associate professor at the University of Hong Kong (~2013).

Gerald Hüther studied at Leipzig University (~1970–1976). He worked at the Max Planck Institute for Experimental Medicine (1979–1989), the University of Göttingen (~1987–2016), and Universitätsmedizin Göttingen (~1995–2016).

Gerald James Larson studied at Union Theological Seminary and Columbia University. A scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, he held professorships at the University of California, Santa Barbara (from 1972) and Indiana University Bloomington (from 1995).
Gerardus van der Leeuw was a religious studies scholar who studied at Leiden University (~1908–1916). He spent his career as a professor at the University of Groningen from 1918 to 1950.
Gerd J. R. Mevissen is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who served as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Free University of Berlin, with affiliations attested in 2017 and 2026.

Gereon Kopf, working in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, studied at Temple University (~1991–1996) and under Yasuo Yuasa. He conducted research at J. F. Oberlin and Nanzan, taught at Hong Kong, and joined Luther College (~1998).

Gergely Hidas is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his DPhil at Balliol College, Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (2002–2008). He was a Khyentse Fellow at Eötvös Loránd University (2007–2014) and a postdoctoral researcher at the British Museum (2014).

Gerhard Meiser was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He completed his education across the Albertus-Magnus-Gymnasium Regensburg, the University of Munich (~1971–1974), the Universities of Belgrade and Sarajevo, the University of Regensburg (~1974–1979), and the University of Freiburg (~1979–1985).

Gerhard Oberhammer, specializing in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, studied at Innsbruck, Paris, and under Erich Frauwallner and V. Raghavan. He held posts at Utrecht University (1961) and the University of Vienna, serving as professor from 1964 to 1997.

Gerhard Wolf, a history and archaeology scholar, studied at Heidelberg University (~1974–1989). He held positions at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1995–1998), Trier University (~1998–2003), and the Max Planck Society (~2003–2020).

Germaine Dieterlen was a scholar of religious studies who studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1935–1941), and under Marcel Mauss (~1937–1940).
Germaine Tillion studied at INALCO, the École du Louvre, and under Marcel Mauss (~1928–1934). She later held a post at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (~1958–1977).
Gernot Böhme was a philosopher who studied at the University of Hamburg (~1960–1965). He subsequently served on the faculty at the Technical University of Darmstadt from ~1977 to 2002.

Gernot Rotter was a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Bonn under Annemarie Schimmel (~1962–1967) and at the University of Tübingen (~1970–1976), later holding a post at the University of Hamburg (~1984–2004).
Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld, an Indologist, studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda (~1946–1974). He later served as associate professor of Indology at the University of Groningen from 1978 to 1986.

Gert Klingenschmitt studied under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, where he also worked as a wissenschaftlicher Assistent (~1968–1976). Specializing in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he held the Indogermanistik chair at Regensburg (1983–2006).

Geshe Jampa Tegchok, a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar, studied at Sera Monastery. He taught at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1971–1982), Nalanda Monastery as abbot (~1982–1993), and the Land of Medicine Buddha (~1995–2001).
Geshe Karma Sonam is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who held posts at Gyume Tantric College (attested 1987) and Sera Monastery (attested 1992).
